stories.notes: Story has empty acceptance criteria and null spec — blank slate. Live preview across GO, UP, and MX platforms involves real-time rendering, iframe sandboxing, state synchronization, and multi-platform behavior. Openspec runs first to elaborate AC and propose technical approach; speckit follows to harden testability, security (iframe sandbox, XSS surface), and edge cases. Priority high because zero AC blocks downstream implementation.

agentContributions.notes: Live Preview is a new capability — the Contentstack Stack is initialized without live_preview config, so no preview data path exists. The attachment point is the Stack initialization in contentstack.ts; downstream, useContent and the content delivery layer must process live-preview URL parameters to fetch draft entries. VCs are derived from the description since ACs are empty, and they stop at our API-call boundary because we cannot reach contentstack.io at test time.

Openspec provided an empty acceptanceCriteria list, so all 10 ACs are original to speckit. I derived them from openspec's note about Stack initialization, useContent parameter processing, and the ContentstackLink component. Key design decisions: (1) AC-1 through AC-3 cover the happy-path flow from Stack init → parameter detection → draft rendering vs published fallback. (2) AC-4 and AC-5 address error handling for malformed params and API failures. (3) AC-6 ensures ContentstackLink works with draft entries, since it's listed as an affected file. (4) AC-7 covers SSR forwarding since these are Next.js apps. (5) AC-8 handles expired/invalid preview tokens specifically, which is a common edge case with Contentstack live preview. (6) AC-9 enforces cross-site consistency since the story title includes [GO, UP, MX]. (7) AC-10 addresses security — URL parameters are attacker-controlled input. CAVEAT: I do not have the file contents, so I inferred the integration points from file names and paths alone. If contentCard.ts defines interfaces that must also carry preview metadata, an additional AC may be needed. If the apps use different Contentstack SDK versions or config patterns, AC-9 may need per-site qualification.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: All four declared files verified as exact matches across gotransit, upexpress, and metrolinx codelines — no unresolved or missing paths. Verification criteria are concrete and observable: VC-1 targets Stack initialization with live_preview config; VC-2 defines a mockable given/when/then for draft rendering with preview params; VC-3 guards published-content regression when params are absent; VC-4 verifies API-call contract (params forwarded when present, omitted when absent). Both agents added non-overlapping value: openspec identified the integration attachment point (contentstack.ts Stack init) and correctly bounded testability at the API-call boundary; speckit hardened with security (URL params as attacker input), error handling (malformed params, expired tokens), SSR forwarding, and cross-site consistency for the [GO, UP, MX] scope. Brownfield policy compliant: empty acceptanceCriteria with acceptanceChanged=false from both agents is the expected redaction — not a defect. Speckit's caveat about potentially needing preview metadata on contentCard.ts interfaces is an ordinary open question a competent writer resolves during implementation. File set is plausible and complete for this change: SDK init (contentstack.ts), content hook (useContent.ts), content interface (contentCard.ts), and consuming component (ContentstackLink.tsx).
